assertionResults.reason: On a fresh browser run against the restored dev harness, opening the Queue tab never exposed any DOM-visible loading or skeleton UI before settled queue content appeared. Even after attempting a deterministic observation technique by injecting a 2s delay for /api/ops/email-queue fetches within the isolated browser session, the Queue tab showed settled KPI tiles and rows immediately, with no skeleton markers, aria-busy region, progressbar, or loading text visible in the DOM. The browser also captured no queue network requests during the tab switch, so the loading state could not be observed through the real surface.

frictions.description: The initial queue tab switch completed fast enough that no transient loading state was human-observable, so an in-session fetch delay was attempted for /api/ops/email-queue to make any loader visible.
frictions.resolution: Retested in the same fresh isolated session with a temporary 2s browser-side delay on queue fetches and captured before/after screenshots plus DOM inspection.

blockers.description: The dev harness appeared to render queue content without an observable queue fetch on tab switch, preventing direct verification of a queue loading indicator from network activity.
blockers.quickFixAttempted: Inspected tracked network requests, injected a 2s delay for /api/ops/email-queue in the isolated session, and checked DOM markers such as skeleton classes, aria-busy, progressbar roles, and loading text; none became visible.

summary: VAL-Q-006 failed: queue loading UI was not observable on the restored dev harness during a fresh browser run, including after a deterministic delayed-fetch retry. Settled queue content was visible, but no skeleton/loading indicators were captured. Additional console evidence showed a hydration mismatch warning during the run.
